correctness.rationale: The full assumptions and normalizations are explicit. Exact capillary finite-depth dispersion yields derivative F(k)=1-3sk²+(1-sk²)q(kH), strictly decreasing from 2 to -2 on the entire instability interval. Thus there is exactly one global growing peak. At it, beta=(1+q)/(3+q), and measured eta=2 tanh(x)/(3+q), strictly increasing from zero to 2/3. The inverse formulas give a two-sided existence/uniqueness proof, including strict boundaries. Exact edge asymptotics are checked algebraically. The standalone bounded numerical optimizer and reconstruction tests cover 76 direct and 63 synthetic cases but are not used to infer infinity-domain assertions.

value.rationale: The fastest-growing wavenumber and exponential rate are natural observable quantities in linear instability. Recovering two hidden physical parameters from only these peak statistics, with a sharp universal realizability region and finite-depth/deep-layer conditioning boundary, is a complete structural inverse problem rather than a routine fixed parameter numerical evaluation. Both strict geometry and reconstruction persist across all allowed positive densities and tensions; the results are useful for exact ideal-model consistency and parameter inversion.
